## Introduction


MAP policy promotions are a puzzle for any brand that sells through retailers and its own Shopify store. You need a reason for shoppers to buy now, and the obvious lever, a lower price on the page, is the one the policy is there to limit.


It's easy to end up choosing between no promotion at all and a promotion you hope nobody flags. Neither is a plan.


There's a third route. Build offers where the price you advertise doesn't move, and the value comes from somewhere else.


This guide covers six of them. We're[Playably](https://playably.ai/) , so one of the six is ours, a conditional cashback rebate where shoppers pay full price.


One thing up front: we aren't lawyers, and this isn't legal advice. MAP policies are written differently, so the last section lists the questions to take to your own counsel before any offer goes live.


### Key Takeaways


- MAP policy promotions work best when the advertised price stays unchanged.
- Gifts, perks, access and shipping add value without touching the price shown.
- Playably runs conditional cashback rebates where shoppers pay full price at checkout.
- How a policy treats any offer depends on its wording, so ask counsel.
- Bring your policy text to the demo call and to your lawyer.


## What a MAP Policy Covers


A minimum advertised price policy is a rule a manufacturer or brand sets for the resellers that carry its products. It names the lowest price they may show in ads, listings and other public places.


It's about the advertised price. The policy owner writes the terms, so the policy owner decides what counts as advertising and what counts as a price reduction.


That's why two brands can read the same promotion differently. One policy may say a lot about free gifts and bundles, another says nothing at all.


Brands that also sell direct on Shopify often hold their own store to the same line. Undercutting your retail partners on your own site can strain those relationships.


If you're tired of the[discount fatigue](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/discount-fatigue) that comes with constant markdowns anyway, MAP is a useful forcing function. It pushes you toward offers that add value instead of subtracting price.


## Why a Percentage Off Is the Wrong Starting Point


A visible percentage off or a slashed price is a direct way to change what a shopper sees. It's the kind of change MAP policies are written to address.


Codes depend on the policy. Whether a code shown in the cart, on a product page or in an email counts as advertising is something the policy wording decides.


The six offers below share one design rule. The price you advertise stays where it is, and the reason to buy comes from something else.


Whether each one fits your policy is a separate question. We'll flag it on every offer, and our breakdown of[cash back vs discount codes](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/cash-back-vs-discount-codes) covers the margin side.


## 1. A Gift With Purchase


Add a product, sample or accessory to qualifying orders. The advertised price of the main product doesn't change.


Pick a gift that makes the main product more useful, so the offer reads as value rather than clearance. It also tends to[increase average order value](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/increase-average-order-value) when shoppers add to reach a threshold.


Check your policy for language on free goods. Some policies address gifts with purchase directly, so read the wording before you advertise the gift alongside the price.


## 2. Free Shipping


Waive shipping on qualifying orders or above a threshold. The product price stays as listed.


It's simple for shoppers to understand and easy to run on Shopify. It still costs real money on every order, so model it the way you would any other offer.


Check whether your policy says anything about shipping. Your policy is the one that decides.


If you use free shipping to rescue carts, our guide to[abandoned cart recovery without discounts](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/abandoned-cart-recovery-without-discounts) has other options.


## 3. Loyalty Points and Member Perks


Reward purchases with points, tiers or members-only perks, with no change to the listed price.


Points pay back later, so the shopper's reason to buy today is the progress, not a lower number on the page. Our guide to[gamified loyalty program strategies](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamification-strategies-for-loyalty-programs-keeping-customers-coming-back) covers how to make progress feel like a reward.


Check how your policy treats points that convert to money off a later order. Some policies treat redeemable value differently from perks like early access.


## 4. Early Access and Limited Editions


Give your email list or members first access to a launch, a restock or a limited colourway, sold at the full advertised price.


Scarcity and status do the work a discount would otherwise do. Nothing about the price changes, because the offer is the access itself.


The list that gets early access has to come from somewhere, and[gamified email capture](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamified-email-capture) is one way to grow it.


Access changes no price, but confirm with counsel if a limited edition is sold through retail partners as well as your own store.


## 5. Full-Price Bundles Built Around a Use Case


Group products that belong together, such as a starter kit or a refill set, and sell the bundle at the sum of its advertised prices or at its own full price.


The value is convenience and curation. The shopper gets the right combination in one click, and it's one of the plays in our[Black Friday 2026 full-price guide](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/black-friday-2026-without-discounting-10-full-price-plays-and-the-numbers-behind-them) .


Bundles deserve a careful read, because a bundle priced below the sum of its parts can look like a price cut. Ask counsel how your policy treats bundle pricing before you set one.


## 6. A Conditional Cashback Rebate


This is the offer Playably runs.


Shoppers buy at full price during the campaign window and get auto-entered. If a real, published trigger event hits, such as a sports result or a weather event, Playably pays them 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal, usually within days.


At checkout, the price is the full price. The offer is a chance at the whole order back, tied to a moment your shoppers already follow, and the[upcoming offers page](https://playably.ai/pages/upcoming-offers) shows the kinds of moments Playably models.


Playably insures and hedges the payout, so the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin. Playably carries the payout, so your store never books the liability.


How a MAP policy treats a post-purchase rebate is a question for that policy's wording and for counsel. Bring it to your lawyer and to the Playably team before you plan a campaign around it.


The published results show what a full-price rebate can do for sales.


Jordan Craig's NEWYORKFREE NFL Draft Rebate saw baskets 34% bigger than the store average, at full price. Read more on the[Jordan Craig case study](https://playably.ai/pages/jordancraig-case-study) .

## Questions to Take to Your Counsel


Before any MAP policy promotion goes live, put these questions to your own lawyer, with the policy text in front of them.


1. Which channels count as advertising under this policy, including our own store, email and social?
2. Does the policy say anything about gifts with purchase, bundles or free shipping?
3. How does the policy treat value delivered after purchase, such as points or a rebate?
4. Does the policy apply to our direct-to-consumer store, or only to resellers?
5. Do any retail partner agreements add terms beyond the policy itself?


Then bring the same policy to the Playably team.[Book a demo](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) and the team walks through the trigger, the build and what a capped campaign would look like for your store.


Playably handles the legal work behind its own rebate offers. How your MAP policy, or a manufacturer's policy you sell under, applies to a campaign is a question for your counsel.


## Conclusion


MAP policy promotions don't have to mean no promotions. They mean offers where the advertised price stays put and the value comes from a gift, a perk, access, shipping or a chance to win the order back.


Start with the offer that fits your policy most cleanly, and check the rest with counsel before you run them.
